headlines.text: That Wednesday in 2022, the AEW World Heavyweight Title found a new home as Jon Moxley vs. Bryan Danielson battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.05 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. Moxley put Danielson to sleep with a rear choke on the stage to become a three-time AEW World Champion, capping the tournament that followed the vacating of the title weeks earlier.

On this day in 2022, the ROH World Heavyweight Title found a new home as Chris Jericho vs. Claudio Castagnoli battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.86 ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. Jericho snuck in a low blow the referee missed, then finished Castagnoli with the Judas Effect to win the ROH World Title ? his eighth world championship overall.

That Wednesday in 2022, there was a changing of the guard for the AEW World Tag Team Titles as The Acclaimed vs. Swerve in our Glory battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.26 ? a good, competitive contest ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. The Acclaimed avenged their All Out loss, with Max Caster hitting the Mic Drop on Swerve Strickland to dethrone Swerve In Our Glory and capture their first AEW World Tag Team Championship.

secondaries.text: Turning the clock back to 2022: PAC vs. Orange Cassidy clashed for the AEW All-Atlantic Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.41.

On a Wednesday in 2022, back when Toni Storm vs. Athena vs. Britt Baker vs. Serena Deeb fought tooth and nail for the AEW Women's World Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 5.83. For Athena, it marked a first real shot at championship gold.
